reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm target engagement for either CTLA-4 or VEGF. Cannot assess whether ipilimumab engaged CTLA-4 or bevacizumab engaged VEGF. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers reported to assess downstream biology changes. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (OS) failed with HR 0.94, p=0.383. The combination arm showed no benefit over monotherapy (OS 20.1 vs 20.4 months). Secondary endpoints PFS and response rate also failed. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The combination arm had higher grade 3-5 AEs (58% vs 39%), particularly hypertension (35% vs 1%), which could have impacted treatment delivery. However, the trial appears adequately powered and conducted over 5 years, suggesting sufficient follow-up time.

failure_modes.evidence: The combination failed to improve OS, PFS, or response rate despite theoretical rationale that anti-angiogenic therapy should enhance immune infiltration. This suggests the assumed biology (enhanced T-cell activation through vascular normalization) did not translate to clinical benefit.
